diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: For each n>=1 the nodes are the original R-modules A_(n+1), B_(n+1), C_(n+1), A_n, B_n, C_n and endpoint zero modules. Horizontal maps f_k:A_k->B_k and g_k:B_k->C_k (k=n,n+1), and the unique zero endpoint maps, have the domains/codomains and row exactness assumed in the Statement.
alpha_(n+1):A_(n+1)->A_n, beta_(n+1):B_(n+1)->B_n, gamma_(n+1):C_(n+1)->C_n are names for the existing transition maps. All three arrows point downward from larger to smaller index.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The supplied def-inverse-system-and-inverse-limit-of-modules defines transitions from M_j to M_i for j>=i; the theorem Statement assumes three such inverse systems.

diagram_math_checks.relation: beta_(n+1) composed with f_(n+1) equals f_n composed with alpha_(n+1); gamma_(n+1) composed with g_(n+1) equals g_n composed with beta_(n+1).
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are exactly the morphism compatibility squares in the Statement short exact sequence of inverse systems; L1 supplier thm-inverse-limits-are-left-exact step 1.1 explicitly uses this convention.

diagram_math_checks.relation: For b in E_(n+1)=g_(n+1)^(-1)(c_(n+1)), g_n(beta_(n+1)(b))=gamma_(n+1)(c_(n+1))=c_n. Hence beta restricts to E_(n+1)->E_n.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Right-square commutativity plus compatibility of c in inverse limit, as used in unchanged proof step 1.2. No transition-map surjectivity is asserted by the figure.
